fields.description:
## Problem

The MCP server's code workspace is cloned once and never updated, so gates read a tree that drifts from `main` indefinitely.

The workspace is docker volume `gerrit_mcp_code`, mounted at `/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` and passed as both `MCP_CODE_DIR` and `REBAR_ROOT` (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:390-417`). `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` treats a checkout as present when `.git` exists and `HEAD` resolves (`:127-130`), so `provision_code()` returns immediately for any present checkout (`:175-181`). Nothing fetches. `autodeploy.sh` advances a *separate* mirror at `/var/lib/rebar/mirror` (`:536-540`) and mounts this volume untouched (`:390-417`, `:852-960`).

## Why it is a signing-correctness hole, not just toil

The close path pins `resolve_ref("HEAD", fetch=False)` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:128-143`), verifies at that ref (`src/rebar/_commands/close_autoresume.py:259-279`; `src/rebar/opcert_service/jobs.py:176-187`), then re-resolves **that same pinned SHA** for its post-verify drift check, again without fetching (`transition_close.py:310-323`). The drift check compares the stale tree against itself, so staleness is invisible to it by construction and a `completion-verifier` signature can be minted over a tree that is not what landed.

Attested gate operations that resolve a ref default to `origin/main` and snapshot it (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:112-156`, `188-245`), so a fetch suffices there. Claim-time currency is *not* protected: `current_head_sha` resolves with `fetch=False` (`gate_source.py:89-109`), comparing against a local idea of `origin/main`.

The mechanism for a signed false PASS is demonstrated. An actual instance is not: the one observed incident produced a false FAIL, which is the safe direction.

## Evidence

Reflog on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5` shows a clone at `f1dd41a8f0` (2026-08-27) and thereafter only manual fast-forwards. No automated advance has ever occurred. At the recorded incident the volume was 130 commits behind, and closing `f920-dc37-28e4-4a91` failed with 6 criteria reporting work absent that had in fact merged. Full detail is in this ticket's investigation comment.

## Approach

Put the correctness boundary on the gate operation, not on the deploy tick. A timer-driven refresh bounds drift but never makes a gate fresh at the moment it runs, and it makes correctness depend on a deploy cadence another deployment may not have.

Add a reusable workspace-refresh helper: take the existing checkout lock, require a clean tree, `git fetch origin main`, then `git merge --ff-only origin/main`. Invoke it as a freshness boundary before a certified gate resolves a `HEAD`-based attested ref. Keep an entrypoint refresh as a warm-up so drift cannot accumulate, but do not rest correctness on it.

The fetch needs a bounded retry window, because Gerrit mirror replication to GitHub takes 20-25 seconds. A gate fired right after a merge can legitimately find the commit missing; that is a wait, not a failure.

**Fail closed.** Unreachable remote, exhausted retries, dirty tree, or an impossible fast-forward means the gate refuses with no signature. It must never fall back to the stale tree — that is this bug reproduced inside its own fix. A dirty or diverged workspace is never mutated, matching the existing `fail-loud-no-auto-restart` posture.

**Portability.** The trigger is the gate operation itself, plus the server lifecycle. That holds under any CI provider or none. A GitHub Actions workflow or Gerrit hook as the only trigger would fail `project.portability`.

## Scope

- A reusable workspace-refresh helper.
- The gate seam invoking it before resolving a `HEAD`-based attested ref.
- `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` warm-up refresh of an existing valid `MCP_CODE_DIR`.
- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` — the workspace, the drift check, the manual break-glass.

## Testing strategy

TDD, failing test first in each case. Tests build a local repo whose `HEAD` is behind its remote and drive the boundary directly, with no LLM call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A certified gate invoked against a workspace behind `origin/main` verifies the advanced tree. Verified by a test placing `HEAD` behind the remote, then asserting the SHA resolved after the boundary runs.
- [ ] A clean `MCP_CODE_DIR` behind `origin/main` is fast-forwarded. Verified by that test failing against today's early-return provisioning.
- [ ] A dirty workspace is left byte-identical. Verified by comparing the working tree before the refusal against after it.
- [ ] A diverged workspace is left byte-identical. Verified the same way, with a non-fast-forwardable history.
- [ ] A refusal names its condition. Verified by asserting the failure text distinguishes dirty from diverged from unreachable.
- [ ] A missing workspace is still re-cloned as today. Verified by a test removing the checkout.
- [ ] A workspace whose `HEAD` does not resolve is still re-cloned as today. Verified by a test corrupting `HEAD`.
- [ ] A fetch that cannot reach the target within the retry budget produces no signature. Verified by asserting no attestation is written.
- [ ] A target SHA appearing only after replication lag is waited for. Verified by a test whose fetch succeeds on a later attempt.
- [ ] The refresh emits the workspace SHA with its distance from the target. Verified by reading the emitted diagnostics.
- [ ] Correctness requires no single CI provider. Verified by reading the trigger path for any GitHub Actions or Gerrit dependency.
- [ ] `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` documents the workspace, the drift check, the break-glass. Verified by reading the file.

## Out of scope

Mode A snapshot resolution, which already fetches. The gates' verdict logic. The separate `/var/lib/rebar/mirror`. A store-wide `verified-at-sha` census to find an actual false PASS — that is worth doing, but it is its own unit of work.
